title: Feature Sprocket Sketchbook
content:
Purpose / elevator:
Quick personal sketch for a tiny feature I think could help small product teams prototype response templates and evaluate inference tradeoffs before full integration. Working name: Feature Sprocket (placeholder).

Problem we see:
- Engineers and PMs keep building one-off prompt wrappers and local fixtures to test LLM outputs. Hard to consistently compare latency/cost for variants (e.g., quantized model vs full fp16) and to preview user-facing templates.
- Console UX today exposes models + deployment config but not a lightweight composer that outputs: candidate responses, token/cost preview, and simple rollout gating.

Proposed micro-solution:
- A small in-console sandbox called Sprocket that lets you:
  * Author a response template (instruction + system + few-shot)
  * Add params/variables and example inputs (table-like rows)
  * Select 2-3 model variants and see side-by-side generated outputs
  * Show estimated tokens, estimated cost, and measured latency (from canary bench runs)
  * Save a template and pin it to a feature flag / route as a canary (10% traffic) with an easy rollback

Why this helps:
- Lowers friction to experiment with fallback strategies (cheap model + rerank) and to preview UX copy.
- Gives product folks a repeatable artifact (template + baseline metrics) they can attach to rollouts.
- Encourages cost-aware decisions earlier.

Core UX flows (very rough):
1) Create template: name, description, instruction box, variables list (key + example).
2) Add examples: upload CSV or paste rows. Each row becomes a test case.
3) Pick variants: dropdown to pick model variants (e.g., redwood/gptx-8b-qat, redwood/gptx-8b-fp16, open/model-lite-3b-q4).
4) Run preview: spins up warm mini-bench for each variant, returns sample outputs for first N rows, plus: avg latency, tokens consumed, estimated per-1k cost.
5) Snapshot & Save: store outputs + metrics as a named snapshot. Snapshots are immutable and can be used to create a rollout.
6) Lightweight rollout: from snapshot, choose route (api route id), percentage, and fallback policy (e.g., fallback to cheaper if latency>300ms).

Minimal API / CLI (notes):
- POST /sprocket/templates -> {name, instruction, variables, examples}
- POST /sprocket/templates/:id/preview -> {model_variants: [..], sample_limit: 5}
- POST /sprocket/snapshots -> snapshotId returned
- POST /sprocket/snapshots/:id/rollout -> {route, percent, fallback_policy}

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Authoring UI that accepts templates and example rows (CSV paste)
- Preview across at least 2 model variants with measured latency (synthetic bench) and token estimate
- Ability to save a snapshot and attach it to a simple rollout for a single API route with percentage and rollback toggle
- Snapshot + rollout are visible in Console under a new "Sprocket" list

Metrics to care about (early):
- Time to create a snapshot (median)
- # of snapshots created per team / week
- Snapshot-to-rollout conversion rate (how many snapshots become rollouts)
- Average per-request cost reduction when teams adopt a cheaper variant
- Rollback rate (signals instability or bad UX)

Edge cases & constraints: (brain dump)
- Preview accuracy vs production: bench runs need to be representative; risk of misleading numbers for cold-start heavy models.
- Security: templates may contain customer PII in examples — need redaction guidance and maybe opt-out from retention.
- Permissions: snapshots should respect org/team scoping and not leak between projects.
- Cost: running previews for many variants could be expensive — throttle or quota previews per user.

Open questions / decisions needed: (TODO)
- Is Sprocket a console-only feature or do we expose the API for programmatic tests? (Would be useful for CI.)
- What pricing/accounting model for preview runs? Free credits? chargeable as normal tokens?
- Snapshot retention policy: 90 days or user-configurable?
- Integration with Optimize: can we suggest quantization or batching knobs based on the sample inputs?

Implementation sketch / dev notes:
- Backend: lightweight preview runner that launches small ephemeral pods with selected model variant; warm up with prompt template + examples, run N samples; collect avg latency + token counts. Store metrics in telemetry table + snapshot blob.
- Data model: Template (id, owner, text, variables), Snapshot (templateId, variantResults[] as references to bench runs), Rollout (snapshotId, route, percent, fallback)
- Permissions: reuse console org/route RBAC
- SRE: limit concurrent previews per org to avoid overload during internal hackdays

Risks:
- Users will over-trust preview numbers and deploy incorrectly; need explicit caveats on variance and sample sizes.
- Operational cost may spike if preview is abused; enforce cost guardrails.

Next actions (personal TODO):
- Quick wireframe: two panes (editor / preview table). Sketch on Miro. (task: create Miro board)
- Slack poll to get product & DX vibes: is this useful? (ask @mateo, @sana, @rhea)
- Draft a short RFC for product review (1 page) and link to JIRA-PI-4821.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep scope narrow for MVP: no complex rerank orchestration, just compare model outputs + metrics.
- Consider exporting snapshots as JSON for attaching to PRs so engineers can run the same snapshot locally.

Example user story (for backlog):
- As a PM, I want to create a response template and compare outputs between the default hosted model and a quantized cheaper variant so I can choose a model that balances cost and quality for an assistant feature.
  Acceptance: PM can save a snapshot that shows side-by-side outputs for 3 examples, and the console shows estimated cost delta and avg latency for each variant.

Closing thought:
- This feels like a very high-ROI lean feature that maps to the company thesis (making inference decisions predictable and economical). Build something that nudges teams to measure costs early without forcing infra changes.

Scratchy brainstorm phrases: 
- "snapshot-as-contract" idea (immutable test artifact)
- local->cloud parity: export snapshot to run against local private deployment for parity checks
- quick-rollout templates for marketing experiments (non-dev PMs like simple toggle UI)

End of sketch.
